# Working diagnosis — overnight dispatch handover

Status: working diagnosis for the morning handover. It is based on the repository, the existing
release check, and the release-desk archive requested after checkpoint `c566a2318f7db32dc98d11368a9417b9df099323`.
It is not a production approval and it does not move traffic.

## Bottom line

The evidence does **not** support a service-side backwards reading or a gRPC regression. The closest
event is a **retried older request** (`req-a`, feed B, sequence 40, attempt 2) arriving after the newer
`req-b` (sequence 41). The live Birch panel `p17` painted 40 and then 41, and **suppressed** the retried
40. The only backwards-looking paint in the trace is on the Birch **training simulator** `p71`
(sequence 39), which is not a live board.

The reports are therefore better explained by transport replay plus display/instrumentation issues
than by the service returning a newer reading as an older one. The existing `bench/check.mjs` is green
because it only sums `grpc_error`; it cannot see ordering, freshness, console upload, or hold state.

## Evidence chain

### 1. Service and release check

- `node --test`: 18/18 pass, including REST compatibility, the five-byte frame, `GetReading`,
  `StreamReadings`, source order, unknown-site errors, and the Fleet zero/omitted default of three.
- `operations/dashboard.csv`: edge `grpc_completed` is 480 then 482, and `grpc_error` is 0 in every
  recorded minute. All ingress requests in the archive also carry `grpc_status = 0`.
- `bench/check.mjs` reports `{ "edgeErrors": 0, "decision": "continue" }`. Its implementation only
  inspects the `grpc_error` series. It does not read `console_upload` or `rollout_hold`, and it has no
  notion of freshness, ordering, or a stale display.

**Interpretation:** a green edge check means transport calls completed without gRPC errors. It is not
evidence that a panel displayed a fresh or correctly ordered reading.

### 2. Ingress trace — the stale retry

| UTC | Connection | Request | Feed | Sequence | Attempt | gRPC status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 22:02:57 | relay-9 | req-a | B | 40 | 1 | 0 |
| 22:03:11 | relay-9 | req-b | B | 41 | 1 | 0 |
| 22:03:14 | relay-2 | req-c | A | 86 | 1 | 0 |
| 22:03:15 | relay-9 | req-a | B | 40 | 2 | 0 |
| 22:03:16 | sim-4 | req-d | B | 39 | 1 | 0 |

`req-a` attempt 2 is the same older sequence (40) as attempt 1, arriving four seconds after the newer
sequence 41. This is a retry/replay at the transport edge, not a new server-ordered reading. The
service is stateless for a retried request: the same request returns the same values. Ordering a
retry against a newer in-flight request belongs to the gateway/transport and the panel.

### 3. Terminal trace — the live panel suppressed it

| UTC | Panel | Feed | Sequence | Request | Event |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| 22:02:58 | p17 | B | 40 | req-a | P (paint) |
| 22:03:12 | p17 | B | 41 | req-b | P (paint) |
| 22:03:14 | p04 | A | 86 | req-c | P (paint) |
| 22:03:14 | p09 | A | 86 | req-c | P (paint) |
| 22:03:16 | p71 | B | 39 | req-d | P (paint) |
| 22:03:17 | p17 | B | 40 | req-a | S (suppressed) |

The live Birch panel `p17` never painted the retried 40 after 41; it suppressed the delivery. The
backwards-looking 39 belongs to the **training** simulator `p71`. The trace is sampled by panel, not
by request, so it establishes what those panels did, not that every live panel was sampled.

### 4. Alias and inventory — why the field note is ambiguous

- `operations/registry.csv` says the **older** `B-12` alias was **"Birch training"** (a previous
  handheld label). The **current** `Birch` assignment is `B-12 plus B-13`, with one returned notebook.
- The archive inventory has Birch live on `relay-9` panels `p17` and `p23`, Alder live on `relay-2`
  panels `p04` and `p09`, and Birch training on `sim-4` panel `p71`.
- The field addendum says `B-12` uses a UTC+01 wall clock that was 52 seconds fast at 22:10Z
  (±12 s), and notebook times were rounded to the minute. The corrected/rounded time is consistent
  with the 22:03Z events, but the addendum explicitly cannot establish whether the board was `p17`
  or the adjacent simulator.

**Interpretation:** "Saw 40 again after 41?" is not attributable to the live Birch board from the
record. It may be the adjacent training simulator, or a practice board carrying the older `B-12`
label. The author's name must not be used in an incident summary until that is resolved.

### 5. The likely "stuck" symptom

The field addendum records that the **B-13 uploader was unplugged for the whole rehearsal** and its
screen retained no local recording. A live panel whose uploader is absent can keep showing its last
painted value; that is a plausible cause of "stuck" and is not a server response regression. It is an
instrumentation/uploader gap, not a reason to change service code.

### 6. Fallback capacity

`CAP-08` (signed 22:19Z) gives Cedar the **only REST overflow lane from 06:00 to 06:30Z**. No second
lane is commissioned. A hold may **park** an affected pilot without moving traffic to REST. The
release owner can change a booking after talking to Cedar; the request has not been made, and no field
authority has accepted a production switch.

## Confidence and limits

- **High confidence:** the recorded ingress/terminal sequence, the zero gRPC errors, the alias
  mapping, and that live `p17` suppressed the stale retry.
- **Medium confidence:** the attribution of the field note to the training simulator or an untracked
  practice board. The record cannot distinguish `p17` from the adjacent simulator.
- **Not established:** a maximum stale interval. The dispatch note says nobody agreed one tonight.
  Without it, "stale" cannot be converted into a measured pass/fail threshold.
- **Instrumentation gaps:** `p23` (a live Birch panel) is not represented in the sampled terminal
  trace; B-13's uploader has no local recording; the release check ignores upload/hold/order/freshness.

## Decision implications

- Do not widen traffic on the green edge count alone.
- Do not carry the "stuck"/"went back" quantity onto the morning board as a measured value.
- Keep the clean Alder cohort live, park Birch pending observation, and preserve Cedar's booked REST
  overflow lane. The detailed morning plan and widen/reverse gates are in `HANDOVER.md`.
- Service code, protocol field numbers, REST routes, deployments, and traffic remain untouched. Only
  the release owner can move traffic.

Deployment and traffic remain with the release owner.

- The edge completed 480 then 482 calls with **zero** gRPC errors; every archived ingress request

Only after all of the following are measured and recorded by the next shift:

1. Both live Birch panels (`p17` and `p23`) show monotonic feed sequences, with no lower sequence

2. Any duplicate/retry after a newer sequence is suppressed by the panel, as `p17` did at 22:03:17.

- A live panel paints a lower sequence after a higher one, or a stale retry is not suppressed.

- The field alias/time cannot be resolved for the board in question, or the incident summary would

- Measured traffic exceeds the site's reservation, the deployed build does not match the replay, or

- No freshness threshold is agreed, or the release owner does not approve the change.

From the repository root:

```sh

# Overnight dispatch — initial written assessment

Status: working diagnosis before the shift-boundary archive requests. This is not a production
approval and it does not move traffic.

## What is established from the repository at this shift boundary

- The current release tests pass: `node --test` reports 18/18 passing, covering REST compatibility,
  the five-byte gRPC frame, `GetReading`, `StreamReadings`, the Fleet zero/omitted default of three,
  source order, and unknown-site errors.
- `bench/check.mjs` reads `operations/dashboard.csv` and sums only the `grpc_error` series. It reports
  `edgeErrors: 0` and `decision: "continue"`. That check does **not** evaluate the `console_upload`
  or `rollout_hold` rows, nor does it test ordering, freshness, or a backwards reading.
- The 22:02/22:03 edge counters are 480 and 482 completed calls with zero errors. The same minute
  records one console panel upload (`Birch/2`) and a scheduler-planned `rollout_hold` of 0 sites.
- The current Fleet planning baseline (`planning/plan.json`) selects Alder + Birch for W1 and
  Birch + Cedar for W2, with Dune on REST in both windows. The plan is a planning baseline, not a
  deployment.
- The released service behaviour is the 2026-11-10 correction: an omitted or zero `StreamReadings`
  limit means the first three readings in source order. The old comment in `proto/energy.proto` is
  stale by explicit design; the proto file is deliberately unchanged.

## Working diagnosis (to be checked against the archive)

The report is not yet evidence of a service-side backwards reading. "Stuck" and "went back" are
operator descriptions, and the only supporting note is a field-notebook entry tied to the older
handheld label `B-12`, from a practice board, at a device-local time. The current registry maps
`Birch` to `B-12` plus `B-13` and records one returned notebook. A display/console or alias/timestamp
explanation is at least as plausible as a server regression, and the existing release check cannot
distinguish them because it ignores the console-upload and hold rows.

The unresolved question is whether a monotonicity/freshness expectation was actually agreed. The
dispatch note says no maximum stale interval was agreed tonight, so "went backwards" cannot be
turned into a specific freshness failure without a source record.

## What must not happen before the evidence is read

- Do not widen the rollout on the strength of the green edge error count.
- Do not carry the "stuck"/"went back" quantity onto the morning board as a measured value.
- Do not change service code, protocol field numbers, REST routes, or traffic. Only the release
  owner can move traffic.
- Do not use the field note's author's name in an incident summary until the terminal/alias is
  confirmed.

## Next evidence to request

The release desk archive is the authoritative next read: inventory (alias crosswalk), ingress
(gateway trace), terminal (operator-console trace), field (calibration and ticket amendment), and
reservation (fallback booking). The final handover will record which archive items were read, what
they established, and what remains an instrumentation gap.

# Working diagnosis — overnight dispatch handover

Status: working diagnosis for the morning handover. It is based on the repository, the existing
release check, and the release-desk archive requested after checkpoint `c566a2318f7db32dc98d11368a9417b9df099323`.
It is not a production approval and it does not move traffic.

## Bottom line

The evidence does **not** support a service-side backwards reading or a gRPC regression. The closest
event is a **retried older request** (`req-a`, feed B, sequence 40, attempt 2) arriving after the newer
`req-b` (sequence 41). The live Birch panel `p17` painted 40 and then 41, and **suppressed** the retried
40. The only backwards-looking paint in the trace is on the Birch **training simulator** `p71`
(sequence 39), which is not a live board.

The reports are therefore better explained by transport replay plus display/instrumentation issues
than by the service returning a newer reading as an older one. The existing `bench/check.mjs` is green
because it only sums `grpc_error`; it cannot see ordering, freshness, console upload, or hold state.

## Evidence chain

### 1. Service and release check

- `node --test`: 18/18 pass, including REST compatibility, the five-byte frame, `GetReading`,
  `StreamReadings`, source order, unknown-site errors, and the Fleet zero/omitted default of three.
- `operations/dashboard.csv`: edge `grpc_completed` is 480 then 482, and `grpc_error` is 0 in every
  recorded minute. All ingress requests in the archive also carry `grpc_status = 0`.
- `bench/check.mjs` reports `{ "edgeErrors": 0, "decision": "continue" }`. Its implementation only
  inspects the `grpc_error` series. It does not read `console_upload` or `rollout_hold`, and it has no
  notion of freshness, ordering, or a stale display.

**Interpretation:** a green edge check means transport calls completed without gRPC errors. It is not
evidence that a panel displayed a fresh or correctly ordered reading.

### 2. Ingress trace — the stale retry

| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 22:02:57 | relay-9 | req-a | B | 40 | 1 | 0 |
| 22:03:11 | relay-9 | req-b | B | 41 | 1 | 0 |

| 22:03:16 | sim-4 | req-d | B | 39 | 1 | 0 |

sequence 41. This is a retry/replay at the transport edge, not a new server-ordered reading. The
service is stateless for a retried request: the same request returns the same values. Ordering a
retry against a newer in-flight request belongs to the gateway/transport and the panel.

### 3. Terminal trace — the live panel suppressed it

| UTC | Panel | Feed | Sequence | Request | Event |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| 22:02:58 | p17 | B | 40 | req-a | P (paint) |
| 22:03:12 | p17 | B | 41 | req-b | P (paint) |
| 22:03:14 | p04 | A | 86 | req-c | P (paint) |
| 22:03:14 | p09 | A | 86 | req-c | P (paint) |
| 22:03:16 | p71 | B | 39 | req-d | P (paint) |
| 22:03:17 | p17 | B | 40 | req-a | S (suppressed) |

backwards-looking 39 belongs to the **training** simulator `p71`. The trace is sampled by panel, not
by request, so it establishes what those panels did, not that every live panel was sampled.

### 4. Alias and inventory — why the field note is ambiguous

- `operations/registry.csv` says the **older** `B-12` alias was **"Birch training"** (a previous
  handheld label). The **current** `Birch` assignment is `B-12 plus B-13`, with one returned notebook.
- The archive inventory has Birch live on `relay-9` panels `p17` and `p23`, Alder live on `relay-2`
  panels `p04` and `p09`, and Birch training on `sim-4` panel `p71`.
- The field addendum says `B-12` uses a UTC+01 wall clock that was 52 seconds fast at 22:10Z
  (±12 s), and notebook times were rounded to the minute. The corrected/rounded time is consistent
  with the 22:03Z events, but the addendum explicitly cannot establish whether the board was `p17`
  or the adjacent simulator.

**Interpretation:** "Saw 40 again after 41?" is not attributable to the live Birch board from the
record. It may be the adjacent training simulator, or a practice board carrying the older `B-12`
label. The author's name must not be used in an incident summary until that is resolved.

### 5. The likely "stuck" symptom

The field addendum records that the **B-13 uploader was unplugged for the whole rehearsal** and its
screen retained no local recording. A live panel whose uploader is absent can keep showing its last
painted value; that is a plausible cause of "stuck" and is not a server response regression. It is an
instrumentation/uploader gap, not a reason to change service code.

### 6. Fallback capacity

`CAP-08` (signed 22:19Z) gives Cedar the **only REST overflow lane from 06:00 to 06:30Z**. No second
lane is commissioned. A hold may **park** an affected pilot without moving traffic to REST. The
release owner can change a booking after talking to Cedar; the request has not been made, and no field
authority has accepted a production switch.

## Confidence and limits

- **High confidence:** the recorded ingress/terminal sequence, the zero gRPC errors, the alias
  mapping, and that live `p17` suppressed the stale retry.
- **Medium confidence:** the attribution of the field note to the training simulator or an untracked
  practice board. The record cannot distinguish `p17` from the adjacent simulator.
- **Not established:** a maximum stale interval. The dispatch note says nobody agreed one tonight.
  Without it, "stale" cannot be converted into a measured pass/fail threshold.
- **Instrumentation gaps:** `p23` (a live Birch panel) is not represented in the sampled terminal
  trace; B-13's uploader has no local recording; the release check ignores upload/hold/order/freshness.

## Decision implications

- Do not widen traffic on the green edge count alone.
- Do not carry the "stuck"/"went back" quantity onto the morning board as a measured value.
- Keep the clean Alder cohort live, park Birch pending observation, and preserve Cedar's booked REST
  overflow lane. The detailed morning plan and widen/reverse gates are in `HANDOVER.md`.
- Service code, protocol field numbers, REST routes, deployments, and traffic remain untouched. Only
  the release owner can move traffic.

# Morning handover — Fleet rehearsal

Prepared by the overnight dispatch lead for the next shift. **No production traffic has been moved,
no service code has been changed, and no protocol field number or REST route has been touched.**
Deployment and traffic remain with the release owner.

## Bottom line

The overnight report is best explained by a **retried older request plus a display/uploader and
alias/timestamp problem**, not by a gRPC service regression:

- The edge completed 480 then 482 calls with **zero** gRPC errors; every archived ingress request
  returned `grpc_status = 0`.
- A retried `req-a` (feed B, sequence **40**, attempt 2) arrived after the newer `req-b` (sequence
  **41**). The live Birch panel `p17` had already painted 40 then 41, and it **suppressed** the retry.
- The only backwards-looking paint in the trace is sequence **39** on the Birch **training**
  simulator `p71`, not on a live board.
- The field note is tied to the **older `B-12` "Birch training"** alias, uses a UTC+01 clock that was
  52 seconds fast (±12 s), and is rounded to the minute. The addendum cannot establish whether the
  reporter saw `p17` or the adjacent simulator.
- The **B-13 uploader was unplugged for the whole rehearsal** and retained no local recording. That
  is a credible cause of a "stuck" screen and is an instrumentation gap, not a service regression.
- `bench/check.mjs` is green only because it sums `grpc_error`; it ignores `console_upload`,
  `rollout_hold`, ordering, and freshness. It cannot be used to widen a rollout on its own.

The detailed evidence chain is in `handover/DIAGNOSIS.md`; the archived source records are in
`handover/archive/`.

## Morning plan (proposal, subject to release-owner approval)

Start with the clean cohort and preserve the only fallback lane:

| Time (UTC) | Site | Action | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 06:00–06:30 | Cedar | **overflow** | Save/use the only booked REST overflow lane (`CAP-08`). This is a scheduling booking; any traffic switch still needs the release owner. |
| 06:10 | Birch | **park** | Hold the affected pilot and show an honest holding state. A park does **not** move traffic to REST. |
| — | Alder | keep live | The clean cohort: Alder feed A painted sequence 86 on both live panels `p04` and `p09`. |
| — | Dune | REST | R1 build remains ineligible; `OPS-17` moves its R2 upgrade to after W2. |

The committed dry-run proposal is `handover/proposal.json`:

```json
{
  "startUtc": "06:10",
  "birch": "park",
  "cedar": "overflow"
}
```

`06:10` is inside Cedar's only overflow window (`06:00–06:30Z`, `CAP-08`). The scheduling dry-run
receipt is `handover/booking-receipt.json`. It covers scheduling only; trial and production approval
remain separate.

### Window shape after the park

| Window | gRPC selection | Used / available | Priority | Notes |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| W1 baseline if Birch is clear | Alder + Birch | 9 / 10 | 20 | Planning baseline. |
| W1 with Birch parked | Alder | 5 / 10 | 11 | Cedar's REST overflow lane is a fallback, not a gRPC capacity reservation. |
| W2 baseline if Birch clears | Birch + Cedar | 8 / 8 | 17 | `NET-31` has already reduced W2 available capacity to 8. |
| W2 with Birch still parked | Cedar | 4 / 8 | 8 | Alder + Cedar would be 9 units and does not fit W2. |

The unit figures come from the existing planning baseline and are not changed here. The park is a
hold, not a capacity reservation or a traffic switch.

## What would make us widen

Only after all of the following are measured and recorded by the next shift:

1. Both live Birch panels (`p17` and `p23`) show monotonic feed sequences, with no lower sequence
   painted after a higher one.
2. Any duplicate/retry after a newer sequence is suppressed by the panel, as `p17` did at 22:03:17.
3. The B-13 uploader is connected and healthy, or its panel is explicitly excluded and the remaining
   panel has a live terminal capture. No selected live panel may be represented only by a screen with
   no local recording.
4. A freshness threshold is explicitly agreed and recorded. None was agreed overnight; do not invent
   one in the incident summary.
5. Measured traffic is within the site's reservation, the replayed build matches the observed build,
   and `node handover/replay.mjs` still returns `ok: true`.
6. The release owner approves the traffic change after talking to Cedar about the only fallback lane.

If those hold, the W1 baseline (Alder + Birch) can be restored and the W2 baseline (Birch + Cedar) can
run. If they do not hold, keep Birch parked. Widening is never justified by the green edge counter
alone.

## What would make us reverse or hold

- A live panel paints a lower sequence after a higher one, or a stale retry is not suppressed.
- A selected live panel has no uploader, no terminal capture, or no usable local recording.
- The field alias/time cannot be resolved for the board in question, or the incident summary would
  need the reporter's name to make sense.
- Measured traffic exceeds the site's reservation, the deployed build does not match the replay, or
  the replay fails.
- No freshness threshold is agreed, or the release owner does not approve the change.

Then park that site and keep the rest of the cohort unchanged. Moving a site to REST is a per-site
traffic switch that only the release owner may approve. A W1 rollback does not force a W2 change.
Dune stays REST until an R2 deployment is recorded and replayed, per `OPS-17`.

## Replay for the next shift

From the repository root:

```sh
node handover/replay.mjs
```

Expected result: exit 0 and a JSON receipt with `ok: true`, `tests.pass: 18`, `tests.fail: 0`, zero
edge errors, the zero/omitted limit both returning three readings in source order, the live `p17`
suppression, the training simulator paint, and the proposal inside Cedar's lane.

The replay is read-only: it runs the accepted test suite, starts the service and REST baseline on
ephemeral local ports, and re-checks the archived records. It does not deploy, switch traffic, or
change the service. A committed copy of its output is `handover/replay-receipt.json`; it can be
regenerated at any time.

## Archive provenance and open items

The shift-boundary checkpoint is `c566a2318f7db32dc98d11368a9417b9df099323` (the initial committed
assessment). The requested archive topics were inventory, ingress, terminal, field, and reservation;
their bodies are preserved verbatim under `handover/archive/`. The next shift can request the same
read-only topics from the desk and compare them with those snapshots.

Open items for the morning:

- Which board the field note saw: live `p17`, or the adjacent training simulator `p71`. The record
  cannot decide; do not name the reporter in the incident summary until it does.
- The terminal trace does not represent live Birch panel `p23`; treat that as an instrumentation gap
  for any widening decision.
- No maximum stale interval was agreed. The morning board must show "holding" rather than a number it
  cannot trust.
- Cedar's booking change has not been requested from the release owner; `CAP-08` is the only lane and
  no second lane is commissioned.

## Authority and scope

This handover is a recommendation. It does not accept a source, approve a proposal, promote a
result, deploy a build, or move traffic. The release owner owns production changes; field operations
own site actions; scheduling owns only the dry-run booking. The approved service is not changed in
this rehearsal.
